records.source: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־תָב֣וֹא אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָ֑ה וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֖הּ וְיָשַׁ֥בְתָּ בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when you come into the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as an] inheritance, and you take possession of it and dwell in it,
pieces: When you have come into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you for an inheritance, and have taken possession of it and settled in it,

L.1: And it shall be, when you come into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and live in it,

R.1: Soon you will enter the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to be your own. You will take it over and settle there.

decisions.choice: the last laws of the long section that began at 12:1
decisions.reason: The laws Moses began to give at 12:1 end with two acts of worship at the sanctuary: bringing the first of the harvest (verses 1-11) and declaring that the third-year tithe has been given (verses 12-15). Both are spoken prayers of thanks for the land. Verses 16-19 then close the whole section.

decisions.choice: after the land is taken and settled: the first harvest there, and each harvest after it
alternatives: a single ceremony at the first harvest in the land
decisions.reason: The rite is set for the time after Israel has taken the land and settled in it, when its fields first yield a crop. The law does not say whether it was done once or every year. The command to bring the first of the harvest to the LORD each year (Exodus 23:19; 34:26) suggests it was repeated.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share of land held by a family and passed down
decisions.reason: The word names property that comes to someone as a lasting share, usually land handed down in a family. The land is the LORD's gift to Israel to hold for good (4:21; 15:4).

decisions.choice: to be your own
decisions.reason: Readable says what an inheritance is here: land given to Israel to keep. Literal and Balanced keep "inheritance".

records.heading: The first fruits

records.source: וְלָקַחְתָּ֞ מֵרֵאשִׁ֣ית׀כָּל־פְּרִ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר תָּבִ֧יא מֵֽאַרְצְךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָ֖ךְ וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ בַטֶּ֑נֶא וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: and you will take from [the] first of all [the] fruit of the ground which you bring in from your land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, and you will put [it] in a basket, and you will go to the place which will choose Yahweh your God to make dwell his name there.
pieces: take some of the first of every crop the ground produces, which you gather from the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. Put it in a basket and go to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

L.2: that you shall take some of the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, and you shall put [it] in a basket and go to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there.

R.2: Then take some of the first crops you harvest from the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. Put them in a basket. Take the basket to the place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: some of the first: a share taken from the first produce to ripen
decisions.reason: The word means the first or the best part. "From" shows that a portion is taken, not the whole crop. The first of the harvest belonged to the LORD (18:4; Exodus 23:19; Numbers 18:12-13), and giving it acknowledged that the whole harvest came from him.

decisions.choice: a basket: a woven basket for carrying produce
decisions.reason: The same word appears in the blessing and curse on "your basket and your kneading bowl" (28:5, 17). The offering is carried by hand, a small gift that stands for the whole harvest.

decisions.choice: the place he will choose to make his name dwell: the one sanctuary
decisions.reason: As in 12:5 and 12:11, the worshiper does not offer at any local shrine but at the single place the LORD chooses, where his name is present among his people.

decisions.choice: every crop the ground produces / crops you harvest
decisions.reason: "Fruit of the ground" means all that the land yields, not only fruit from trees. Balanced and Readable say "crop"; "bring in" is gathering in the harvest. Literal keeps the Hebrew words.

records.source: וּבָאתָ֙ אֶל־הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו הִגַּ֤דְתִּי הַיּוֹם֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ כִּי־בָ֨אתִי֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה לַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ לָ֥תֶת לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will go to the priest who will be in the days those and say to him, I declare today to Yahweh your God that I have come into the land which swore Yahweh to our fathers to give to us.
pieces: Go to the priest who is in office at that time and say to him, 'Today I declare to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I have come into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to our ancestors to give us.'

L.3: And you shall go to the priest who is [in office] in those days and say to him, 'I declare today to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I have come into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to our fathers to give us.'

R.3: Go to the priest who is serving at that time. Tell him, 'Today I am announcing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I have come into the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} solemnly promised our ancestors {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give us.'

decisions.choice: the priest who is in those days: whoever is serving as priest at the time
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the priests and judges at the sanctuary in 17:9 and 19:17. The law looks ahead to a time when Moses and Aaron are gone and others serve.

decisions.choice: I declare: I state openly, as a public confession
decisions.reason: The verb means to tell or make known. The worshiper's gift comes with a spoken statement that the promise to the ancestors has been kept: the land has been given.

decisions.choice: I have come ... to give us: one person speaks for the whole people
decisions.reason: Each worshiper speaks in the first person, as though he himself had entered the land, and counts himself among the "us" to whom it was promised. Every generation is to say it of itself, as 5:3 speaks of the covenant made "with us, all of us here alive today".

decisions.choice: your God
decisions.reason: The worshiper speaks to the priest, so "your God" means the priest's God, the God of all Israel. The ancient Greek translation reads "my God" here, which may be a smoothing of the harder wording. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: [in office] / in office / serving
decisions.reason: "Who will be in those days" means the one who holds the office then. Literal brackets the supplied words; Balanced says "in office" without brackets, and Readable says "serving".

records.source: וְלָקַ֧ח הַכֹּהֵ֛ן הַטֶּ֖נֶא מִיָּדֶ֑ךָ וְהִ֨נִּיח֔וֹ לִפְנֵ֕י מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will take the priest the basket from your hand and set it down before [the] altar of Yahweh your God.
pieces: The priest will take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.4: And the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.4: The priest will take the basket from you and put it down in front of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: the priest sets it down; in verse 10 the worshiper is told to set it down
decisions.reason: Verse 10 tells the worshiper, "you shall set it down before the LORD your God". The two verses may describe two moments of one rite, the worshiper laying the basket down after the priest has received it, or one act told twice, once from the priest's side and once from the worshiper's. The meaning of the rite is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the altar: the altar at the chosen place
decisions.reason: This is the altar where the burnt offerings were made at the place the LORD chooses (12:27). Setting the basket before it presents the gift to the LORD himself.

records.source: וְעָנִ֨יתָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֜ לִפְנֵ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אֲרַמִּי֙ אֹבֵ֣ד אָבִ֔י וַיֵּ֣רֶד מִצְרַ֔יְמָה וַיָּ֥גָר שָׁ֖ם בִּמְתֵ֣י מְעָ֑ט וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֕ם לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל עָצ֥וּם וָרָֽב׃
records.gloss: And you will answer and say before Yahweh your God, An Aramean perishing [was] my father, and he went down to Egypt and sojourned there with men of fewness, and he became there a nation great, mighty and numerous.
pieces: Then you shall speak up and declare before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God: 'My ancestor was an Aramean, a wanderer. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner, few in number, and there he became a great nation, strong and numerous.

L.5: And you shall answer and say before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, 'A wandering Aramean [was] my father, and he went down to Egypt and sojourned there with few people, and there he became a nation, great, mighty and numerous.

R.5: Then say these words in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God: 'My ancestor was a homeless wanderer from Aram. He went down to Egypt with only a few people and lived there as a foreigner. But there his family grew into a great nation, strong and with many people.

decisions.choice: wandering: a man adrift, without land, close to being lost
alternatives: an Aramean tried to destroy my father
decisions.reason: The verb means to perish or to be lost. It is used of animals that have strayed (1 Samuel 9:3, 20; Jeremiah 50:6; Ezekiel 34:4, 16) and of people who perish (4:26; 8:19-20). Here it describes the ancestor himself: a man without a homeland, straying from place to place and in danger of ruin. That fits Jacob's life: he fled from Esau to Aram (Genesis 27:43; 28:5), served Laban there for twenty years, came back to Canaan, and was driven by famine to go down to Egypt (Genesis 42-46). Some take the stress to be on the danger, "perishing" or "ready to perish", as in the famine when his sons went to buy grain "so that we may live and not die" (Genesis 42:2; 43:8). An old Jewish reading, found in the Passover Haggadah, takes the word as "destroying" and reads "an Aramean (Laban) tried to destroy my father"; but this form of the verb does not mean "destroy" elsewhere, and "my father" is the one who goes down to Egypt in the next clause. The Hebrew phrase is short, and no reading is certain.

decisions.choice: an Aramean ... my father: Jacob, whose family came from Aram
decisions.reason: The ancestor who "went down to Egypt" is Jacob (Genesis 46:3-7). He is called an Aramean because his mother and his wives came from the family in Aram (Genesis 25:20; 28:2-5), and he lived there for many years (Hosea 12:13, "Jacob fled to the field of Aram"). Abraham too came from Haran in Aram (Genesis 11:31; 24:4, 10), so the words may also look back to the family's origin as a whole. Israel's story begins with a landless outsider, not a great people.

decisions.choice: with men of fewness: few in number
decisions.reason: "Men of fewness" means a small group of people, as in Genesis 34:30. Jacob's household that went to Egypt numbered seventy (10:22; Genesis 46:27), which became a great nation (Exodus 1:7).

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for an outsider living among another people. In Egypt Jacob's family lived without land or full rights of their own, as Genesis 15:13 foretold and Exodus 22:20 recalls.

decisions.choice: ancestor
decisions.reason: "My father" here is a forefather, not the speaker's own father. Balanced and Readable say "ancestor"; Literal keeps "father".

decisions.choice: a homeless wanderer from Aram; his family grew into
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what a wandering Aramean is, a man from Aram with no settled home, and says that "he became a nation" through his descendants.

records.source: וַיָּרֵ֧עוּ אֹתָ֛נוּ הַמִּצְרִ֖ים וַיְעַנּ֑וּנוּ וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ עָלֵ֖ינוּ עֲבֹדָ֥ה קָשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And treated badly us the Egyptians and afflicted us, and put on us labor hard.
pieces: But the Egyptians mistreated us and oppressed us, and forced hard labor on us.

L.6: And the Egyptians treated us badly and afflicted us and laid hard labor on us.

R.6: But the Egyptians were cruel to us. They made us suffer and forced us to do hard work.

decisions.choice: afflicted ... hard labor: the words of Exodus 1
decisions.reason: The confession uses the words of Exodus 1:11-14, where the Egyptians set taskmasters "to afflict" Israel and made their lives bitter "with hard labor" (also Exodus 6:9).

decisions.choice: us: the worshiper counts himself among the oppressed
decisions.reason: The speaker moves from "my father" to "us". As in verse 3, each Israelite tells the story of the exodus as his own people's story and his own.

records.source: וַנִּצְעַ֕ק אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶת־קֹלֵ֔נוּ וַיַּ֧רְא אֶת־עָנְיֵ֛נוּ וְאֶת־עֲמָלֵ֖נוּ וְאֶת־לַחֲצֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And we cried out to Yahweh [the] God of our fathers, and heard Yahweh our voice and saw our affliction and our toil and our oppression.
pieces: Then we cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our ancestors, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard our cry and saw our misery, our toil and our oppression.

L.7: And we cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our fathers, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard our voice and saw our affliction and our toil and our oppression.

R.7: We cried out for help to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of our ancestors. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard us. He saw how we were suffering, how hard we had to work, and how we were crushed.

decisions.choice: we cried out ... he heard ... he saw: as in Exodus 2-3
decisions.reason: The words follow Exodus 2:23-25 and 3:7-9: Israel cried out, God heard their groaning, saw their affliction, and saw the oppression with which the Egyptians pressed them.

decisions.choice: affliction, toil, oppression: humiliation, exhausting labor and being pressed hard
decisions.reason: The first word is misery or humiliation, the second hard and wearing work, the third pressure, a squeezing or crushing (Exodus 3:9). Together they describe a people worn down.

decisions.choice: heard our cry / heard us
decisions.reason: "Heard our voice" means heard what we called out. Balanced says "cry"; Readable says "heard us" and adds "for help", which is what crying out means here.

records.source: וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נוּ יְהוָה֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם בְּיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּבִזְרֹ֣עַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבְמֹרָ֖א גָּדֹ֑ל וּבְאֹת֖וֹת וּבְמֹפְתִֽים׃
records.gloss: And brought us out Yahweh from Egypt by a hand strong and by an arm outstretched and by terror great and by signs and by wonders.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out of Egypt by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, by great terror, and by signs and wonders.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror and with signs and with wonders.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring us out of Egypt. He did terrifying things, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} worked signs and miracles.

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: God's power at work
decisions.reason: The hand and the arm stand for strength in action. The pair is used again and again of the exodus (4:34; 5:15; 7:19; 11:2).

decisions.choice: great terror: deeds that filled people with fear
decisions.reason: The word is fear or dread, here the awe that the LORD's acts in Egypt caused, both among the Egyptians and in Israel (4:34; 34:12).

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues and other acts of power
decisions.reason: Signs are acts that point to the LORD and show who he is; wonders are acts that astonish. Both name the plagues on Egypt (6:22; 7:19; Exodus 7:3).

decisions.choice: used his great power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of hand and arm as power, as in 11:2.

records.source: וַיְבִאֵ֖נוּ אֶל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּתֶּן־לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And he brought us to the place the this and gave to us the land the this, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.
pieces: He led us to this place and gave us this land, a land that flows with milk and honey.

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.

R.9: He brought us to this place. He gave us this land, a rich land, full of milk and honey.

decisions.choice: this place: the place of worship where the speaker stands, or the land itself
decisions.reason: The speaker stands at the place the LORD has chosen (verse 2), and "this place" may point to it: he brought us here, to his sanctuary. It may also mean the land, as "this place" does in 1:31 and 9:7, and the next clause then says the same thing again in other words.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: Milk comes from herds that have good pasture, and honey from wild bees or from fruit such as dates. The phrase describes the land's richness (6:3; 11:9; Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: a rich land, full of milk and honey
decisions.reason: Readable adds "rich" to say what the picture means, as in 6:3.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֤ה הֵבֵ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־רֵאשִׁית֙ פְּרִ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּה לִּ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהִנַּחְתּ֗וֹ לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֔יתָ לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And now, here! I have brought [the] first of [the] fruit of the ground which you have given to me, Yahweh. And you will set it down before Yahweh your God and bow down before Yahweh your God.
pieces: And now here I have brought the first of the produce of the ground that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have given me.' Then set it down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and bow down in worship before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.10: And now, see, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.' And you shall set it down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and bow down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.10: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, here are the first crops from the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me.' Then put the basket down in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and bow down to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: you have given me, O LORD: the story turns into prayer
decisions.reason: Up to here the worshiper has spoken about the LORD; now he speaks to him. The gift of the land in verse 9 and the gift of its first fruits meet: what the LORD gave, the worshiper brings back to him. His words end with the LORD's name; the rest of the verse is Moses' instruction again.

decisions.choice: set it down: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: See verse 4: the priest sets the basket down there, and the worshiper here.

decisions.choice: bow down: bow low in worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down to the ground before someone greater. Before God it is the posture of worship.

decisions.choice: O LORD / LORD, and the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The name is used as a form of address, so English says "O LORD" at Literal and Balanced and places it early at Readable. The worshiper's words that began in verse 5 end here, after the name.

records.source: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֣ בְכָל־הַטּ֗וֹב אֲשֶׁ֧ר נָֽתַן־לְךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּלְבֵיתֶ֑ךָ אַתָּה֙ וְהַלֵּוִ֔י וְהַגֵּ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּקִרְבֶּֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: And you will rejoice in all the good which has given to you Yahweh your God and to your household, you and the Levite and the sojourner who [is] in your midst.
pieces: And you shall rejoice in all the good things that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given to you and your household, you together with the Levite and the outsider living among you.

L.11: And you shall rejoice in all the good that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given to you and to your household, you and the Levite and the sojourner who [is] among you.

R.11: Then celebrate and enjoy every good thing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you and your family. Let the Levites and the outsiders who live among you celebrate with you.

decisions.choice: rejoice: celebrate with a festive meal at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy rejoicing before the LORD means eating and celebrating together at the place he chooses (12:7, 12, 18; 14:26; 16:11, 14). The first fruits lead to a feast of thanks.

decisions.choice: the Levite and the sojourner: those without land of their own share in the harvest
decisions.reason: The Levites had no share of land (14:27, 29), and the sojourner was an outsider living in Israel without family land. Both are to share the joy of the harvest that the land-holding household enjoys.

decisions.choice: outsider
decisions.reason: The sojourner is a foreigner settled among Israel. Balanced and Readable say "outsider", as in 14:21 and 14:29; Literal keeps "sojourner". Readable uses plurals for the groups.

records.source: כִּ֣י תְכַלֶּ֞ה לַ֠עְשֵׂר אֶת־כָּל־מַעְשַׂ֧ר תְּבוּאָתְךָ֛ בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ת שְׁנַ֣ת הַֽמַּעֲשֵׂ֑ר וְנָתַתָּ֣ה לַלֵּוִ֗י לַגֵּר֙ לַיָּת֣וֹם וְלָֽאַלְמָנָ֔ה וְאָכְל֥וּ בִשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ וְשָׂבֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: When you finish to tithe all [the] tithe of your produce in the year the third, [the] year of the tithe, and you give [it] to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, and they eat in your gates and are satisfied,
pieces: When you have finished setting aside the full tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless and the widow, so that they can eat their fill in your towns,

L.12: When you have finished tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given [it] to the Levite, to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, so that they eat within your gates and are satisfied,

R.12: Every third year is the year of the tithe. In that year, when you have finished setting aside a tenth of all your crops, give it to the Levites, the outsiders, the children without fathers and the widows. Let them eat all they want in your towns.

decisions.choice: the third year, the year of the tithe: the tithe kept in the towns for those in need
decisions.reason: As 14:28-29 sets out, in every third year the tithe is not taken to the sanctuary to be eaten by the family but stored in the towns for the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless and the widow.

decisions.choice: the year of the tithe
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "you shall give the second tithe" in place of "the year of the tithe", reading the same Hebrew letters with different vowels. The Hebrew text is followed. Later Jewish practice spoke of a first, a second and a poor tithe.

decisions.choice: finish: give the whole tithe, holding nothing back
decisions.reason: The verb means to complete. The worshiper's statement in verse 13 depends on it: all the tithe has been handed over.

decisions.choice: one sentence with verse 13
decisions.reason: The "when" clause of this verse is completed by "then you shall say" in verse 13, so the record ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: Every third year is the year of the tithe. In that year ...
decisions.reason: Readable states first what the third year is, then gives the instruction, and uses "a tenth" for the tithe and "children without fathers" for the fatherless, as in 14:22 and 14:29.

records.heading: The tithe of the third year

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ לִפְנֵי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בִּעַ֧רְתִּי הַקֹּ֣דֶשׁ מִן־הַבַּ֗יִת וְגַ֨ם נְתַתִּ֤יו לַלֵּוִי֙ וְלַגֵּר֙ לַיָּת֣וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֔ה כְּכָל־מִצְוָתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתָ֑נִי לֹֽא־עָבַ֥רְתִּי מִמִּצְוֺתֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
records.gloss: and you will say before Yahweh your God, I have removed the holy [portion] from the house and also I have given it to the Levite and to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, according to all your commandment which you commanded me; not I have transgressed [any] of your commandments, and not I have forgotten.
pieces: then say in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God: 'I have removed the holy portion from my house and have given it to the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless and the widow, just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me. I have not turned aside from any of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments, and I have not forgotten them.

L.13: then you shall say before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, 'I have removed the holy [portion] from the house, and I have also given it to the Levite and to the sojourner, to the fatherless and to the widow, according to all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandment that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me. I have not transgressed [any] of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commandments, and I have not forgotten [them].

R.13: Then say in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, 'I have taken out of my house the part that is holy to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I have given it to the Levites, the outsiders, the children without fathers and the widows, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me to do. I have not disobeyed any of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, and I have not forgotten them.

decisions.choice: I have removed: I have cleared it out completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to clear away or remove entirely. Deuteronomy uses it for purging evil from Israel (13:6; 17:7). Here it means none of the holy tithe has been kept back in the house.

decisions.choice: the holy portion: the tithe, which belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: The tithe is holy because it belongs to the LORD (Leviticus 27:30). Keeping it at home would be using for oneself what is his.

decisions.choice: transgressed: stepped over, gone beyond
decisions.reason: The verb means to pass over or cross. Of a command, it is to step past it, to break it or leave it aside (17:2).

decisions.choice: before the LORD: at the sanctuary or in his presence anywhere
decisions.reason: The third-year tithe stays in the towns, but the declaration is made "before the LORD". This may mean at the sanctuary, at the next visit there, or simply as a prayer spoken to the LORD at home. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: my house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "my house": "the house" is the speaker's own home, where the tithe was stored.

records.source: לֹא־אָכַ֨לְתִּי בְאֹנִ֜י מִמֶּ֗נּוּ וְלֹא־בִעַ֤רְתִּי מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ בְּטָמֵ֔א וְלֹא־נָתַ֥תִּי מִמֶּ֖נּוּ לְמֵ֑ת שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י עָשִׂ֕יתִי כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Not I have eaten in my mourning of it, and not I have removed of it [while] unclean, and not I have given of it to [the] dead. I have listened to [the] voice of Yahweh my God; I have done according to all which you commanded me.
pieces: I have not eaten any of it while in mourning, I have not removed any of it while I was unclean, and I have not given any of it for the dead. I have done what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God said; I have done all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me.

L.14: I have not eaten of it in my mourning, and I have not removed any of it while unclean, and I have not given any of it to the dead. I have listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God; I have done according to all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded me.

R.14: I did not eat any of it while I was mourning a death. I did not take any of it out of my house while I was unclean. I did not use any of it in rites for the dead. I have listened to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God and obeyed. I have done all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me to do.

decisions.choice: in my mourning: while in a house of mourning
decisions.reason: A death made a house and those in it unclean (Numbers 19:14), and the food of mourners was unclean (Hosea 9:4). Holy food could not be eaten there.

decisions.choice: removed while unclean: handled the holy portion while ritually unclean
decisions.reason: Holy things were not to be touched by someone in a state of uncleanness (Leviticus 7:20; 22:3-7). The worshiper declares that the tithe was set aside and given in the proper state.

decisions.choice: given to the dead: used in rites for the dead
decisions.reason: This may mean food set out as an offering for the dead, a practice of the nations around Israel (Psalm 106:28, "sacrifices for the dead"). Or it may mean food given for the meal shared with mourners after a death (Jeremiah 16:7). Either way, food holy to the LORD was not to be used for the dead.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what he says (13:19; 15:5).

decisions.choice: done what the LORD my God said / listened ... and obeyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that listening to his voice means doing what he says; Literal keeps the idiom.

records.source: הַשְׁקִיפָה֩ מִמְּע֨וֹן קָדְשְׁךָ֜ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וּבָרֵ֤ךְ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֵת֙ הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תָּה לָ֑נוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתָּ֙ לַאֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃ס
records.gloss: Look down from [the] dwelling of your holiness, from the heavens, and bless your people Israel and the ground which you have given to us, just as you swore to our fathers, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.
pieces: Look down from heaven, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy dwelling place, and bless Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, and the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given us, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised on oath to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.'

L.15: Look down from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel and the ground that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given us, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore to our fathers, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.'

R.15: Look down from heaven, the holy place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} live. Bless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel. Bless the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given us, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised our ancestors with an oath. It is a rich land, full of milk and honey.'

decisions.choice: look down: look down from above with attention
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking down from a height, as the LORD looks down from heaven on people (Psalm 14:2; Lamentations 3:50). Here it asks for his favor.

decisions.choice: your holy dwelling, in heaven: God lives in heaven, while his name dwells at the chosen place
decisions.reason: The worshiper stands where the LORD has made his name dwell (verse 2), but prays to him in heaven. Solomon's prayer holds both together: the LORD hears from heaven the prayers made toward the place of his name (1 Kings 8:27-30).

decisions.choice: the ground: the farmland that yields the harvest
decisions.reason: The word is the soil, the ground that is farmed, as in "the fruit of the ground" (verses 2 and 10). The prayer asks for blessing on next year's crops as well as on the people.

decisions.choice: the land / promised on oath
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "land" for the farmed ground and "promised on oath" for "swore". Readable puts the description of the land in a sentence of its own. The worshiper's words that began in verse 13 end here.

records.source: הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ מְצַוְּךָ֧ לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת אֶת־הַחֻקִּ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֤ וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אוֹתָ֔ם בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: The day the this Yahweh your God [is] commanding you to do the statutes the these and the judgments, and you will take care and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
pieces: Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commands you to keep these statutes and rulings. Be careful to keep them with all your heart and with all your soul.

L.16: This day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is commanding you to do these statutes and the judgments; and you shall be careful to do them with all your heart and with all your soul.

R.16: Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is commanding you to obey these laws and rules. Be careful to obey them with all your heart and with all your being.

decisions.choice: these statutes and judgments: the laws of chapters 12-26
decisions.reason: The pair that opened the laws at 12:1 (and 5:1; 6:1) closes them here. "These" points to everything given since 12:1.

decisions.choice: this day: the day Moses speaks in Moab
decisions.reason: "This day" is the day of Moses' address, when the covenant is set before Israel again before they cross the Jordan (5:3; 29:9-14).

decisions.choice: with all your heart and with all your soul: with the whole self
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind and will; the soul is the living self. Together they mean wholehearted obedience, as in 6:5 and 10:12.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments / statutes and rulings / laws and rules
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this pair in these books. Readable says "being" for "soul", as in 11:13.

records.heading: His treasured possession

records.source: אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה הֶאֱמַ֖רְתָּ הַיּ֑וֹם לִהְיוֹת֩ לְךָ֨ לֵֽאלֹהִ֜ים וְלָלֶ֣כֶת בִּדְרָכָ֗יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֨ר חֻקָּ֧יו וּמִצְוֺתָ֛יו וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֥עַ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh you have declared today to be for you for God, and to walk in his ways and to keep his statutes and his commandments and his judgments, and to listen to his voice.
pieces: Today you have declared that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is your God, and that you will follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, commandments and rulings, and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.

L.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} you have declared today to be your God, and [that you will] walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments, and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice.

R.17: Today you have said that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is your God. You have promised to live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws, commands and rules, and to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says.

decisions.choice: you have declared: you have publicly stated, as one side of an agreement
alternatives: you have caused the LORD to say (that he will be your God)
you have accepted the LORD's word
decisions.reason: This form of the verb "say" is found only here and in verse 18. It is a causative form, and it can be read as "you have declared", "you have proclaimed", or "you have caused the LORD to say", that is, you have had him declare that he will be your God. Read the first way, Israel declares that the LORD is its God (verse 17) and the LORD declares that Israel is his people (verse 18). Read the second way, each side has the other make the promise. In both readings the two verses state the two sides of the covenant.

decisions.choice: to walk, to keep, to listen: what Israel undertakes
decisions.reason: The first phrase, "to be your God", is what the LORD will be; the phrases that follow are what Israel will do. Israel's declaration includes both: the LORD is our God, and we will live by his ways.

decisions.choice: to be your God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: This is one side of the covenant formula, "I will be your God and you will be my people" (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Verse 18 gives the other side.

decisions.choice: [that you will] walk / promised to live
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that show the change of subject; Balanced says "that you will"; Readable makes it a promise Israel has made.

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֞ה הֶאֱמִֽירְךָ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם לִהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־לָ֑ךְ וְלִשְׁמֹ֖ר כָּל־מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh has declared you today to be for him for a people of treasured possession, just as he spoke to you, and to keep all his commandments,
pieces: And today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has declared that you are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} treasured possession, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you, and that you are to keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

L.18: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has declared you today to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, a treasured possession, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you, and [that you are] to keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,

R.18: And today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said that you are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} very own treasure, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you. You must obey all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands.

decisions.choice: has declared: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: The same rare verb as in verse 17, now with the LORD as subject: he states his side of the covenant. See the note there.

decisions.choice: treasured possession: a prized personal property
decisions.reason: The word means something a person owns and values highly, a private treasure (1 Chronicles 29:3). Israel is the LORD's own (7:6; 14:2; Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: the promise at Sinai
decisions.reason: The LORD said at Sinai that Israel would be his treasured possession if they kept his covenant (Exodus 19:5-6).

decisions.choice: and to keep all his commandments: Israel's part, within the LORD's declaration
decisions.reason: The LORD's declaration includes what his people are to do: keep his commandments. Verse 19 goes on with what he will do for them.

decisions.choice: his very own treasure
decisions.reason: As in 7:6, Readable says "very own treasure" for "treasured possession".

records.source: וּֽלְתִתְּךָ֣ עֶלְי֗וֹן עַ֤ל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לִתְהִלָּ֖ה וּלְשֵׁ֣ם וּלְתִפְאָ֑רֶת וְלִֽהְיֹתְךָ֧ עַם־קָדֹ֛שׁ לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: and to set you high above all the nations which he has made, for praise and for a name and for honor, and for you to be a people holy to Yahweh your God, just as he spoke.
pieces: and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set you high above all the nations {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made, to be praised, famous and honored, and that you will be a people holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised."

L.19: and to set you high above all the nations that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made, for praise and for a name and for honor, and [for] you to be a holy people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke."

R.19: He will make you greater than all the other nations {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made. You will receive praise and honor, and your name will be known everywhere. You will be a holy people who belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised."

decisions.choice: to set you high: the LORD's part; high is a description, not a title
decisions.reason: The verb now has the LORD as its subject: he will raise Israel above the nations. The word for "high" is the one used elsewhere as a title of God, "the Most High", but here it describes Israel's place, as in 28:1.

decisions.choice: for praise, for a name, for honor: Israel's renown among the nations
alternatives: for the LORD's praise, name and honor
decisions.reason: The three words say that Israel will be praised, famous and honored among the nations (Zephaniah 3:19-20). In Jeremiah 13:11 the same three words describe what Israel was meant to be for the LORD, so Israel's honor is also his.

decisions.choice: a holy people: set apart to belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Israel is holy because the LORD chose it and set it apart for himself (7:6; 14:2, 21; 28:9; Exodus 19:6).

decisions.choice: the end of the speech Moses began at 5:1
decisions.reason: Moses' second speech, which began at 5:1 and contains the laws of chapters 12-26, ends here. Chapter 27 begins with the narrator's words.

decisions.choice: promised; the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: "As he spoke" refers to his promise, so Balanced and Readable say "promised". The quotation mark opened at 5:1 closes at the end of this verse, where Moses' second speech ends.

decisions.choice: He will make you greater ... You will receive praise and honor
decisions.reason: Readable makes the LORD's promise a sentence of its own and says plainly what "praise, a name and honor" means.
